solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Carol and Jerry, both heartless, resorted to blandishment

indicators.note: sorted again, so the remaining letters are put into a new order
each name loses its central letter, its heart, which in both cases is an R

parts.note: the two names written together, the 'and' simply joining them

explanation.surface: Two people, Carol and Jerry, stripped of feeling, fall back on flattery to get their way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both heartless' takes the middle R from each name, leaving CAOL and JERY; 'resorted' then rearranges those eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name flattery and coaxing talk used to win someone over.

clue.text: Company with exactly what one is looking for to hold two million in pledge

indicators.note: the two pieces hold the millions between them

parts.words: exactly what one is looking for
parts.note: 'it' is the very thing wanted, as in 'that's it'
M is million, so two of them

explanation.surface: A firm that has exactly what a buyer wants pledges two million.
explanation.definitionFit: To bind oneself to a course is to pledge, as a verb.

clue.text: A deer just disturbed rosy flowered plant

indicators.note: the letters of the three words are disturbed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A deer has just disturbed a pink-blossomed shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: The Judas tree bears purplish-pink flowers in spring, before its leaves.

clue.text: Thrash innocent, a saint

parts.note: a lamb is a type of innocence

explanation.surface: Someone beats an innocent person, a saint.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat soundly or criticise harshly, in either sense to thrash.

clue.text: Insurgent, fifty, going after beer, drunk

indicators.note: the numeral comes after the rearranged beer
the beer, once drunk, is jumbled into a new order

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A fifty-year-old rebel chasing beer while drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone rising in arms against authority is a rebel or insurgent.

clue.text: Blow a hot pipe

parts.note: a hook is a curving punch in boxing
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: An instruction to blow through a pipe that is hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow' looks like a verb but is a noun, the boxer's punch.
explanation.definitionFit: A water pipe used for smoking tobacco, its smoke drawn through a bowl of water.

clue.text: Lear's daughter that's broken up loves herb

indicators.note: the pair of loves is split apart by the daughter

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O, so two of them
Regan is one of King Lear's daughters in Shakespeare

explanation.surface: King Lear's daughter, who broke up loves, is likened to a herb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' only links: Regan is the one doing the breaking up, standing between the two loves.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild marjoram, an aromatic herb used in Italian cooking.

clue.text: Author involved in mounting pipsqueak fakery

indicators.note: mounting says the hidden letters are read backwards
involved in says the letters are concealed within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A writer is mixed up in some petty fraud by a nobody.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Author involved' as the definition, but 'involved in' is the hiding signal; 'mounting' reads the hidden run upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Kafka, the Prague-born novelist of The Trial, is an author.

clue.text: Fellow always supporting Welsh town produces irritation

indicators.note: in a down clue the fellow and always sit beneath the town, holding it up

parts.note: Hay-on-Wye, usually called Hay, is a Welsh book town
ever means always

explanation.surface: A man who is forever propping up a Welsh town ends up causing irritation.
explanation.definitionFit: An allergic reaction to pollen inflaming the nose and eyes is an irritation.

clue.text: Originating material for organisms hawk traps caught and gathered up

indicators.note: the word for hawk holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: to hawk is to sell goods

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is read upwards

parts.note: met means gathered together
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A hawk traps its prey, which is caught and collected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hawk' looks like the bird but is the verb to peddle; 'up' works only because this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Undifferentiated cells from which all an organism's specialised tissues develop.

clue.text: Fairy queen circles broad, complete space over stage for opera

indicators.note: the fairy queen's name goes round the word for a woman

parts.note: Queen Mab is the fairy queen of Mercutio's speech in Romeo and Juliet
slang for a woman, as is dame
utter means complete, total
the fly or flies is the space above a theatre stage where scenery hangs

explanation.surface: A theatrical scene: a fairy queen flits around a woman and the whole stage space in some opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broad' is American slang for a woman, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Puccini's opera about the Japanese bride Cio-Cio-San is the title in question.

clue.text: Place that is inches high

parts.note: INS is the abbreviation for inches
tall means high

explanation.surface: A spot described as only inches high, or a measure of height.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that is' merely links definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To set up or position something, such as fitting equipment, is a verb synonym.

clue.text: Meanly taking half levy, revenue's ending butcher's device

indicators.note: only the first half of the word meanly is taken

parts.note: a tax is a levy

indicators.note: only the final letter of revenue's is used

explanation.surface: A miser grabs half of a tax, the revenue's last share, like a butcher with a cleaver.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleaver, the heavy chopping tool a butcher uses on carcasses.

clue.text: Nearly plagiarise quite freely in review

indicators.note: the last letter is dropped, so the word is nearly complete

parts.note: to crib is to copy someone else's work

indicators.note: the letters of quite are moved around freely

explanation.surface: A reviewer accuses an author of almost copying someone else rather freely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' cuts CRIB to CRI; 'freely' rearranges QUITE as TIQUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A critical assessment or essay is a review of a work.

clue.text: Queen manufactured mirage in difficult situation

indicators.note: the letters of mirage are manufactured into a new form

explanation.surface: A queen conjures up an illusion when she is in a tight spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, a bog one sinks into is a predicament or tricky position.

clue.text: Chore mixing clay and iron pigment

indicators.note: the letters of chore are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A painter grinding clay and iron together finds it a chore.
explanation.definitionFit: An earthy pigment is clay coloured by iron oxide, giving yellows and browns.

clue.text: More risky to take doctor for producer of hot air

indicators.note: the riskier word takes the doctor inside itself

parts.note: hairier is informal for more dangerous

explanation.surface: It is more dangerous to take a doctor along for someone who talks hot air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'producer of hot air' suggests a windbag, but it is literal: the appliance blows hot air.
explanation.definitionFit: A blow-dryer for hair literally blows out warm air.

clue.text: Game away is monotonous at first, defending one's area

parts.note: nim is a game of taking counters from heaps
by can mean aside or away, as in 'put by'

indicators.note: the first letter of monotonous

explanation.surface: An away fixture is dull at the start while the side defends its own area.
explanation.definitionFit: The attitude of 'not in my back yard', resisting development near one's home.

clue.text: Perfect fish pursued by small boy

indicators.note: the fish comes first, followed by the boy

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish, a crossword favourite
Al is a short form of the boy's name Albert or Alan

explanation.surface: A perfect scene: a fish being chased by a little boy.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, flawless or exactly as wished for.

clue.text: Spotted flier in America that's left bad guy twisting

indicators.note: the letters of bad guy twist into a new order

explanation.surface: An American insect has abandoned a villain, writhing.
explanation.definitionFit: The American name for the ladybird, a red beetle with black spots that flies.

clue.text: Place having submerged tin works appearing in map

indicators.note: the rearranged tin is placed inside the book of maps

parts.note: an atlas is a book of maps

indicators.note: the letters of tin are worked into another order

explanation.surface: A spot with sunken tin mines shown on a map.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' looks like a noun for mines but is the anagram signal on 'tin'.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary island that sank beneath the sea, a place that went under.

clue.text: Once more upset, god falls on border

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is turned upside down, so read in reverse

parts.note: again means once more
Ra is the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: Again upset, a god falls on the frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: The waterfalls straddle the boundary between the USA and Canada.

clue.text: Pancake's last remnant of kitchen in sudden attack

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the pancake is the definition

indicators.note: that letter goes inside the attack

parts.note: a blitz is a sudden attack

indicators.note: the final letter of kitchen

explanation.surface: The pancake was the last thing left in the kitchen after a sudden raid.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin rolled pancake filled with cheese or fruit, of Jewish cuisine.

clue.text: Tolerated party finale in glum tedium

parts.note: bore means put up with, endured
a do is a party

indicators.note: a finale is the closing part of a show, so only the closing letter of glum is used

explanation.surface: Someone sat through a party's glum end in a state of tedium.
explanation.definitionFit: Weariness from dullness and lack of interest is the meaning shared.

clue.text: Irons out ingredient of wax

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of irons are disordered

explanation.surface: Someone irons out a component of wax.
explanation.definitionFit: Resin from pine is an ingredient of sealing wax and polishes.

clue.text: Disgrace in prison embraced by backsliding boys

indicators.note: the prison is held within the reversed boys
sliding backwards, so the word for boys reads in reverse

parts.note: lads are boys
the can is slang for prison

explanation.surface: Boys who have relapsed into crime end up in prison, a disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backsliding' suggests moral relapse but simply turns the boys round.
explanation.definitionFit: A public outrage or shameful affair brings disgrace.

clue.text: Southern inclination to drink greedily

parts.note: will means wish or inclination

explanation.surface: A Southerner's tendency to gulp drink down.
explanation.definitionFit: To gulp or guzzle liquid, as a pig takes its slops.

clue.text: Appointment aboard U-boat perhaps creates mutiny?

parts.note: in means on board
a U-boat is an example of a submarine, a sub
ordination is appointment to holy orders

explanation.surface: A posting on a German submarine leads to the crew rising up?
explanation.walkthrough: Read in order: ordination 'in sub' gives the pieces; the question mark flags the U-boat as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Defiance of authority by those under command, which on ship is mutiny.

clue.text: Servant takes long time to control

parts.note: a man is a manservant
an age is a long time

explanation.surface: A servant takes ages to gain control.
explanation.definitionFit: To run or direct something is to control it.

clue.text: American pen recreated unlimited black art with most extreme characters

indicators.note: the remaining letters together with art are created anew in a different order
the word black loses its limits, its first and last letters

parts.note: A and Z are the first and last letters of the alphabet

explanation.surface: An American artist reworks black art using the most extreme characters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unlimited' leaves LAC; 'recreated' shuffles LAC with ART to give ALCATR.
explanation.definitionFit: The notorious former island prison in San Francisco Bay, a US penitentiary or pen.
